steps: This video shows how Claude tool use really works: Claude asks, your code checks and runs. A support agent asks TicketFlow to check the status for alice at example dot com.
TicketFlow sends the message to Claude along with a tools array. It defines one tool, lookup customer, with a J S O N input schema where email is required.
Claude does not answer yet. It returns a tool use block containing the email argument, and the stop reason is tool use, not end turn. Claude has asked, but nothing has run.
Before anything touches the database, your dispatcher validates the email. A malformed one, with no at sign, goes back as an error tool result instead of crashing. This one is valid.
The email passes, so TicketFlow runs the query against the customer database. It returns premium tier, with two open tickets.
You append that data as a tool result in a user message and send it back. Now Claude writes the final reply, and the stop reason is end turn.

The support agent gets an answer grounded in live data: Alice is premium with two open tickets. The takeaway: Claude requests tools, and your code validates and executes them. The full walkthrough is in the Gennoor Claude certification course.
